title: Frank Carbone, trumpeter and neighbor
summary: Clarifying the nickname and identity of trumpeter Frank Carbone, who lived across from Stanko and admired Chris Kelly's blues.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Did you mention Carbone did you say?
Yeah, Carbone. We used to call him Kev. Frank Carbone. It was a nickname that we gave him. His name was Frank Thomas, see? But we called him Frank Carbone. Oh, yeah.
You talk about Big Bill's brother? Big Bill's brother.
Yeah, Frank Carbone. And he really played nice trumpet.

He worked for Lettler, Ye, and Phillip. He worked for Lettler, Ye, and Phillip. That's right. And he... He used to live on St. Peter, between me and I talked to you. Right next door to us. Across the street from Stanko. Across the street from Stanko. From Stanko.
That's where we were living. That's right. Right across from Stanko. That's where...
There's a lot of jobs with him. Oh, man.
He was one of them that... I'll tell you who he admired. He admired Chris Kelly, because he could play the blues. Oh!
That's the guy I was trying to think about.
He could play the blues. Frank could play the blues.
